title: Permissions-to-Purchase Procedure Manual
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the end-to-end procedures for (1) requesting and granting access/permissions, (2) approving infrastructure or application changes, (3) data handling and retention requirements, (4) procurement and expense approvals, (5) vendor onboarding and management, and (6) travel policies and expense templates. The goal is to reduce time-to-approval while preserving security, compliance, and budgetary controls.

Scope: Company-wide; applies to all employees, contractors, and vendors interacting with Redwood systems or spending Redwood funds. Exceptions require documented approvals per the Exceptions process (Section: Exceptions & Escalation).

Owner and escalation
- Document owner: Finance & Legal (Maya Patel)
- Primary approvers: Cost Center Managers, Team Leads, Procurement (procurement@redwood.com), Security (security@redwood.com) where required
- Escalation path: Manager -> Procurement -> Finance Director -> Legal (for contract review)

Key service-level commitments (SLOs)
- Standard access requests: responded to within 48 business hours (target)
- Emergency access (time-limited): fulfilled within 2 hours with Security on-call approval
- Low-risk purchases (< $5,000): approved within 3 business days
- Mid-tier purchases ($5,000–$50,000): 7 business days (includes procurement review)
- Enterprise or capital purchases (>$50,000): 15 business days plus contract review

Section 1 — Access & Permissions
1.1 Request types- Read-only access (no code/deploy permissions)
- Developer access (repo, CI, staging)
- Production runbook access (view-only or sudo)
- Emergency/Just-in-time (JIT) elevated access

1.2 Process
1) Submit request in Access Portal (link: /access-portal) with justification, duration, and owner.
2) Auto-assign to Cost Center Manager for first-level approval.
3) Security reviews requests that include admin, production, or data-sensitive scopes.
4) Access granted via IAM automation; requestor receives email and ticket closure.

1.3 Approval matrix (table)
| Resource type | Typical approver | Security review required? | Duration cap |
|---------------|------------------|---------------------------|---------------|
| Dev repo (read/write) | Team Lead | No (unless cross-team) | 12 months |
| Prod cluster (view) | Service Owner | Yes | 90 days |
| Prod cluster (sudo) | Engineering Manager + Security | Yes | 8 hours (emergency) / 30 days (standard) |

Section 2 — Change Management (infra & app)
2.1 Change categories- Standard change: routine, pre-authorized (minor infra config, non-customer impacting).
- Minor change: scheduled, low-risk, requires peer review.
- Major change: high-risk, impacts customers or capacity; requires CAB approval and rollback plan.

2.2 Change request procedure
1) Open a Change Request (CR) in the Change Tracker with: summary, impact assessment, test plan, rollback plan, owner, schedule.
2) Automated risk classification determines routing.
3) Required approvers: Service Owner, SRE (for infra), Product when customer-facing, Security for sensitive data changes.
4) CAB review (weekly) for Major changes; emergency CAB convenes within 4 hours for SEV-level changes.

2.3 Acceptance gates and telemetry- Pre-deploy checks: unit/integration test pass, canary policy defined, monitoring playbook attached.
- Post-deploy verification: latency/error budget checks at 5/30/120 minutes.

Section 3 — Data Management
3.1 Classification- Public: safe to publish.
- Internal: operational data not for public disclosure.
- Confidential: PII, customer data, secrets.

3.2 Data handling rules- Confidential data must be stored in encrypted buckets with restricted IAM roles.
- Retention: default retention 3 years for logs; sensitive customer data retention per contract or legal requirements.
- Data deletion: documented request via Data Life-cycle form; audited by Data Steward.

3.3 Data access reviews- Quarterly access review for Confidential data owners.
- Automated attestations: managers receive monthly lists for attestation.

Section 4 — Procurement & Expenses
4.1 Thresholds and approvals- < $5,000: Team Lead approval.
- $5,000–$50,000: Cost Center Manager + Procurement review.
- > $50,000: Procurement + Finance Director + Legal review.
- Subscriptions: annual contracts on auto-renew require 60-day procurement notice for vendor review.

4.2 Spend request template (required fields)- Requestor name, cost center, business justification, vendors considered, budget code, expected contract length, SLAs required, security requirements, estimated total cost.

4.3 Purchase process (numbered steps)
1) Complete Spend Request form and attach vendor quotes.
2) Procurement validates vendor (KYC, security questionnaire) and confirms budgets.
3) Finance issues PO or processes corporate card charge for approved purchases.
4) Contracts > $50k routing to Legal for redlines; procurement coordinates signature.

4.4 Expenses and travel- Per diem: Domestic $120/day, International varies by region (see travel region table).
- Expenses to submit within 14 days of trip end; late submissions require manager exception.
- Corporate card policy: personal charges strictly prohibited; disputed charges must be reported within 30 days.

Section 5 — Vendor Management & Onboarding
5.1 Vendor risk tiers- Tier 1: Enterprise platform providers (high risk) — must pass SOC2/ISO audit and security questionnaire.
- Tier 2: SaaS tools handling internal data — security review and limited access.
- Tier 3: Low-risk vendors (office supplies) — Procurement-only review.

5.2 Onboarding checklist (table)
| Step | Responsible | Artifacts |
|------|-------------|----------|
| Intake & initial assessment | Requesting team / Procurement | Spend Request, vendor contact |
| Security questionnaire | Procurement + Security | Completed questionnaire, evidence (SOC2 report) |
| Contract negotiation | Procurement + Legal | Signed contract, SOW |
| Billing & PO setup | Finance | Vendor W-9 / tax info, PO |
| Access provisioning | Procurement + IT | Service account, least-privilege roles |

5.3 Contract clauses to require- Data processing agreement (DPA), breach notification timeline (<=72 hours), right to audit, termination for convenience, data return/deletion on termination.

Section 6 — Travel policy highlights
- Pre-approval: All business travel must have pre-approval via Travel Request form.
- Class of travel: Economy standard for flights under 6 hours; business for flights >6 hours pre-approved by manager.
- Hotel: Up to mid-tier business hotels; exceptions require justification.
- Insurance: Company-provided travel insurance for international trips.

Templates and artifacts (links)- Spend Request form: /templates/spend-request
- Access Request form: /templates/access-request
- Change Request template (CR): /templates/change-request
- Vendor Security Questionnaire: /templates/vendor-security-q

Exceptions & Escalation
- Any deviation from thresholds or access duration must include an Exceptions Request form and be routed to the documented approver.
- High-risk exceptions escalate to the Executive Risk Committee.

Audit, reporting, and continuous improvement- Quarterly internal audits of access, procurement, and travel spend.
- Key metrics: average approval time, percent of purchases with required security review, vendor onboarding time, travel spend per head.
- Roadmap items: automate spend vs. budget alerts, integrate access attestation with payroll/HR for leavers.

Appendix A — Quick reference tables
Approval matrix (summary):
| Amount band | Required approvers |
|------------|---------------------|
| <$5k | Team Lead |
| $5k–$50k | Cost Center Manager, Procurement |
| >$50k | Procurement, Finance Director, Legal |

Access SLO quick reference:
- Standard: 48 business hours
- Emergency: 2 hours

Contact list
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.com
- Security: security@redwood.com
- Finance: finance-ops@redwood.com
- Travel & expenses: travel@redwood.com

Change history

End of document
